basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: An interaction is the exchange between parties over a channel, made of turns; a single message (WM-REC-003) is one of its parts.
It records what was observed and referenced, never a permission, access or audit decision.
Platform acceptance of a send is not delivery, and an engagement signal is not proof of comprehension.
Gaps, late or duplicate turns stay visible and marked rather than absorbed.

may: Open an interaction and bind its channel endpoints.
Append turns and resolve thread membership.
Record delivery evidence with its source.
Link the interaction to related records such as orders, cases or requests.
mustNot: Treat opens or clicks as proof that a person understood a message.
Expose blind-copied participants or redacted spans to other participants.
Send an outbound turn without a resolvable permission basis reference.
Present a partial record as complete.
requiresHuman: Closing an interaction with a legal or contractual outcome.
Disclosing an interaction to a third party.
Handling a dispute about whether a revocation was received.

considerations: Communications are private; content and traffic data need protection.
Service interactions should treat people with dignity, including clear disclosure when they are talking to an agent.
Unwanted contact burdens people and must respect their objection.
affectedParties: Human and software agents handling it

items: An interaction has a channel, participants, a thread or session identifier and a sequence of turns.
Confused with a single message, a support ticket, a case and a call recording.
Misrouting of confidential turns to the wrong participant.
Hidden gaps that misrepresent what was said.
Contact without permission or after withdrawal.
TM Forum TMF683 Party Interaction Management API.
RFC 6120 Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP).
